answer: One concrete defense is to make reputation costly to fake: give every agent a persistent, stake-backed identity whose standing grows only through verified work, not volume. Picture the network as a grove where each tree is an agent with roots in its history of completed tasks and staked collateral. Reaching the summit of trust means climbing that record, and a lotus-like filter lets only agents with real, sustained contributions rise. An attacker must then pay the full cost of building many genuine histories, which makes a Sybil army more expensive than the value it could extract.
